method: Candidate counterfactual rollouts from training-split states; LLM predicts next recorded response category

mdp.decision_epoch: one simulated treatment decision; irregular clinical time is not represented
mdp.reward: 1 for predicted TF-Tumor Free, 0 for predicted WT-With Tumor; abstention has no reward
mdp.treatment_constraints: class combinations observed at least min_action_support times in training split; no dose actions
mdp.safety_constraints: only dataset-supported action classes; no toxicity, contraindication, or dose-safety model exists

policy_training: none; these are random and historical-frequency baselines for Objective 3, not an RL-optimized policy

random_supported.toxicity_cost_wellbeing_evaluation: not possible: these outcomes are absent from the dataset

historical_most_common.toxicity_cost_wellbeing_evaluation: not possible: these outcomes are absent from the dataset

status_conditioned_historical.toxicity_cost_wellbeing_evaluation: not possible: these outcomes are absent from the dataset

observed_holdout_check.evaluation: factual observed-action predictions on held-out test patients
limitations: This evaluates observed action/outcome pairs, not alternative-treatment effects.
Undated treatments can still hide intervening actions in dated_event_only_candidate records.
The target is the next qualifying recorded response, not a fixed-horizon response.
Small support and class imbalance can make the estimate unstable.

warnings: Every rollout is a model-generated hypothesis, not an observed or causal treatment effect.
Action support is observational frequency and does not prove clinical appropriateness or treatment overlap.
The candidate initial states include incomplete treatment histories flagged in source data.
No toxicities, costs, quality-of-life values, or calibrated confidence are available; safety and multi-objective utility cannot be evaluated.
Do not use this prototype for patient care or real treatment recommendations.
